source: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 9 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 9
knowledgePattern: Factor a high-power integer equation and count signed ordered solutions
solution:
The two cubic identities reduce the left side to (x3+y3)(x3−y3)=x6−y6. Put a=|x| and b=|y|. Then a and b are nonnegative integers with a > b and (a3−b3)(a3+b3)=63.

The positive factor pairs in increasing order are (1,63), (3,21) and (7,9). Adding each pair and halving would give a cubed equal to 32, 12 or 8. Only 8 is an integer cube, giving a = 2 and b = 1.

Thus x can be either 2 or −2 and y either 1 or −1, independently. All four ordered pairs work. Answer E.

hints.title: Multiply the familiar pairs first
hints.body: Group (x+y) with (x2−xy+y2), and (x−y) with (x2+xy+y2). Expand each pair.
hints.recap: Factoring or regrouping can reduce the number of terms before expanding further.
hints.pitfall: The signs of the mixed terms differ in the two pairs.
hints.pause: Write the equation using your two shorter factors.

recall.reminder: Factoring or regrouping can reduce the number of terms before expanding further.

hints.title: Use factor pairs of 63
hints.body: Because only even powers remain after multiplication, first let a=|x| and b=|y|. For the two factors a3−b3 and a3+b3, list the possible positive factor pairs of 63.
hints.recap: A list of all divisors gives all possible positive factor pairs.
hints.pitfall: The factors must give whole-number cubes when you add and subtract them.
hints.pause: Find the possible magnitudes, then restore every permitted sign of x and y.

recall.reminder: A list of all divisors gives all possible positive factor pairs.
